title: How do we make a fifteen degree angle by cutting thirty in half?
description: A thirty degree angle made by cutting sixty in half, then cut in half once more with arcs from the two arms. Two matching triangles show the new line splits thirty into two equal angles. Keeko's doubt, drawing an arc from D, is struck.
teaching_notes: One idea: the same cutting in half works again on the thirty degree angle, with arcs from points at equal distance from A. Watch for students who draw the arc from a point not on the arm at that distance.

source: Construct a 15° angle at a point A on a line, using only a r
video_script.why: The child sees that the cutting in half can be repeated to get a smaller exact angle.
video_script.substitution: The first arc from A cuts both arms at the same distance, so AB equals AE.
video_script.anchor: A line with the point A marked on it, a ruler and a compass.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko draws the arcs from B and D. But AD is not equal to AB, so the two triangles do not match and AF does not cut the angle in half.
video_script.payoff_line: Angle F eigh B is fifteen degrees.

final_answer.spoken: angle F eigh B is fifteen degrees

maths_rules: Construct ∠CAB = 60° with two equal arcs and bisect it, giving ray AD with ∠DAB = 30°.
The first arc from A cuts AD at a point E, so AB = AE (radii of one arc).
Arcs from B and E with one radius meet at F inside ∠DAB. Join A and F.
AB = AE, BF = EF, AF is common, so triangle ABF is congruent to triangle AEF by SSS.
So ∠FAB = ∠FAE, and each is half of 30°, which is 15°.
Slip: arcs from B and D, where AD is not equal to AB, do not give matching triangles.
video_script.design: One line, one point A and the arcs from the last video. A new pair of arcs sits inside the thirty degree angle. The slip is drawing from D instead of E.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks we can draw the arcs from B and D.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But eigh D is not equal to eigh B, so the two triangles do not match.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The line would not cut the angle in half. The two points must be the same distance from eigh, so we use B and E.
